card.title: YDSE — fringe width from path difference

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Huygens rebuilds every wavefront from secondary wavelets — reflection, refraction and TIR all follow geometrically. Coherent superpositions interfere: Young's double slit splits one wavefront into two coherent sources whose path difference paints bright/dark fringes. Single-slit diffraction spreads light into a central maximum twice as wide as the rest. Polarization filters the transverse vibration direction; Brewster's angle reflects fully polarised light.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: YDSE: path difference = d·sinθ · bright: d·sinθ = nλ · fringe width β = λD/d  ·  single slit minima: a·sinθ = nλ (central max 2× wide)  ·  Brewster: tanθ_p = μ  ·  Huygens: every point = new wavelet source

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Sustained interference needs coherent, monochromatic, same-polarisation sources with a small slit gap (d ~ mm for visible light). Fringe formula assumes D ≫ d (small-angle geometry). Brewster reflection polarises completely only at θ_p with unpolarised incidence on dielectrics.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: White-light YDSE: central white fringe, coloured edges (β ∝ λ — red spreads widest). Narrower slit → wider diffraction spread (uncertainty in disguise). Polaroids in sunglasses kill horizontal glare (reflected light is partially polarised). Soap films and oil slicks: thin-film interference, same physics.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: YDSE fringe positions: geometry gives path difference S₂P − S₁P ≈ d·y/D (D ≫ d); bright when it equals nλ → y_n = nλD/d, so consecutive fringes space β = λD/d. Measure β, D, d → λ = βd/D — the classic wavelength-measurement experiment.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Ray optics is the λ → 0 limit — fringes vanish from its picture entirely. Real slits have finite width (interference × diffraction modulation). Partial coherence washes fringes out; lasers, not candles, make clean patterns.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Huygens → Snell: wavelets crossing the boundary at different speeds tilt the reconstructed front by exactly sin i/sin r = v₁/v₂. YDSE bright condition from path difference; single-slit minima by pairing wavelets across the slit width (first minimum where halves cancel: a·sinθ = λ). Brewster: reflected + refracted rays perpendicular → tanθ_p = μ.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: β = λD/d solves every YDSE numerical — identify which variable is asked. 'Missing fringes' = interference maxima coinciding with diffraction minima. Polarisation questions: Brewster tanθ_p = μ; crossed polaroids transmit nothing.
